marks.gloss_en: an etrog of an asheira is unfit
כתיב הכא לחם עוני, וכתיב התם והיה באכלכם מלחם הארץ: מה להלן משלכם ולא משל מעשר, אף כאן משלכם ולא משל מעשר (35a.13-35b.1; ואיתימא Rav Yeimar bar Shelamya)
מתקיף לה רב פפא: dough has 'your dough', the etrog has 'for yourselves'; but matza -- is 'your matza' written?
Rav Pappa: granted dough -- 'the first of YOUR dough' is written
R' Asi said: per R' Meir one does not fulfil with a second-tithe etrog, per the Sages one does -- the shape of the monetary-standing dispute, so he is its author (תסתיים)
per R' Meir: with an etrog of second tithe a person does not fulfil his obligation on the festival
תנן: של תרומה טמאה פסולה -- fine for the permission-to-eat view; but for the monetary-standing view, why? he burns it under his cooking (= p_masika_tachat_tavshilo)
(entertained) whoever requires permission to eat does not require monetary standing, and whoever requires monetary standing does not require permission to eat
an etrog of orla is unfit
on permission to eat, all agree that it is required
second tithe in Jerusalem has permission to be eaten
per R' Meir: with matza of second tithe a person does not fulfil his obligation on Pesach
ואימא פלפלין; כדתניא -- say it is pepper, whose wood and fruit also taste alike, as R' Meir's baraita teaches
R' Meir: 'any tree' already implies a food tree; 'a food tree' teaches a tree whose wood and fruit taste alike

התם משום דלא אפשר: ננקוט חדא -- לא מינכרא לקיחתה; ננקוט תרי או תלתא -- אחד אמר רחמנא ולא שנים ושלשה פירות: with pepper the mitzva is impossible -- one is not noticeable, and the Torah said one fruit, not two or three
אטו שאר פירות לית בהו גדולים וקטנים, תמימין ובעלי מומין?! -- do other fruits not have large and small, whole and blemished? the comparison singles out nothing
אלא הכי קאמר: עד שבאין קטנים, עדיין גדולים קיימים (= p_rabbi_hakhi_kaamar)
Rabbi: do not read hadar but hadir (a pen)
'the fruit of a beautiful tree' is a tree whose wood and fruit taste alike
R' Abbahu: do not read hadar but haddar (that dwells)
